_spec.purpose: Automation change trail. Phase 8's upgrade-engineer logs every machine change here. Each run's set reverts as one upgrade(<date>): commit.

entry_schema.addresses: optional list of retro.py defect slugs this upgrade FIXES. This is how a repeat offender is closed out: by shipping a change that claims it, never by editing the detector.

entries.upgrade: scripts/script_check.py: Gate 0's mechanical half. Hard-fails a dangling claim-id, a line citing a CUT claim, Ray gone longer than one whole beat, and Ray absent from the middle third.
entries.verified_by: python3 scripts/script_check.py --self-test -> exit 0, all 6 cases ok. Each guard broken in turn on a patched copy (MAX_RAY_GAP_S=999, NOT_USABLE=(), inside=[1], dangling=[]) -> exit 1 'THE GATE IS WRONG' every time, and the case naming that guard is the one that goes red. Against the real artifacts: runs/2026-08-01/script.json exit 0 (longest Ray silence 11.4s), runs/2026-08-02/script.json exit 1 (longest silence 27.9s from 9.5s, NONE in 17.7-35.4s), which is the defect the flow critic and the scorer found after a full render.

entries.upgrade: vo_gemini.py uses the newest TTS model and sends STRUCTURED direction instead of a bare style string. Every take now carries an Audio Profile, a Scene, Director's Notes and a TRANSCRIPT heading, with an explicit instruction that only the transcript is spoken. Inline performance tags are validated against a known set and the tag that caused the original complaint is banned outright.
entries.verified_by: Re-synthesized all 12 lines of case 0002 with per-character briefs and 7 tagged lines. vo_soundcheck --episode PASSED all 12 with zero overruns, which is the proof the model PERFORMED the direction rather than reading it aloud: a take that speaks its own notes runs long and trips OVERRUN, and the soundcheck self-test has a fixture for exactly that case. Episode rebuilt end to end: 48.87s, mux -20.2 dB, render gate PASS at 1080x1920. The banned tag raises on construction; an undocumented tag warns rather than failing, so a new tag costs a warning and not a dead run. CORRECTION, same day: this entry originally claimed those takes ran on gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview. THEY DID NOT. vo_cast.py set DISPATCH_GEMINI_TTS_MODEL to gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts at module scope and vo_gemini is imported later, so the older model won on import order alone and every take of case 0002 was 2.5-pro. Nothing failed, so the wrong model shipped and got written down as fact. Fixed in the entry below.

entries.upgrade: One default for the TTS model, and a run gate that reads back what actually resolved. vo_cast.py's module-scope os.environ.setdefault was silently outranking vo_gemini's newer default purely by import order, so the pipeline used gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts while every report said 3.1-flash. The override is deleted, vo_gemini owns the default alone, and check() now asserts the RESOLVED model rather than the intended one.
entries.verified_by: Before: importing vo_cast then vo_gemini resolved gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts. After: resolves gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview, asserted by reading vo_gemini.MODEL back rather than by reading either comment. The guard was then proven RED in the direction that matters: running check() with DISPATCH_GEMINI_TTS_MODEL=gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts fails the 'TTS model is gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview' row and prints the model it caught. This is the whole class of bug the run reports could not see, because a downgraded model renders clean and passes every objective gate.

entries.upgrade: THE CASTING LAW, in code. Owner verdict on Dee, twice: 'mad robotic', 'no fluctuation'. Two causes were stacked and both are now refused mechanically: a human character cast to a voice whose roster descriptor is flat, and a director's brief that instructs the ABSENCE of prosody. Dee moves from Schedar (descriptor: 'Even') to a voice with a disposition, and her brief stops asking for what it was complaining about.
entries.verified_by: python3 scripts/vo_cast.py --self-test -> exit 0, 11 cases, four of them new and three RED on purpose: a flat-descriptor voice on a human, a style note saying 'no rising intonation', a pace note saying 'monotone'. The Institution is EXEMPT and the self-test proves the exemption still passes, because that character is a phone tree and its blandness is the joke. The live table is checked too, so the gate fails the moment someone re-flattens a brief. Note what the gate deliberately does NOT do: the seven-voice sweep measured 3.46 to 4.12 semitones of pitch variance across every candidate INCLUDING the one the owner called robotic, so the machine cannot rank these and does not pretend to. It refuses the two known causes and leaves the pick to the ear.

entries.upgrade: The take cache keys on the MODEL as well as the brief, and the key is computed in one place. It was written out twice, in cached_duration and in take, and both copies omitted the model, so fixing the model default alone would have replayed every old take off disk under the new model's name.
entries.verified_by: The same line under two models now produces two different cache filenames (fe7ca240e0c4233e vs 743811a6af2f39b8); before the fix it produced one. vo_cast --self-test still exit 0. This was the THIRD instance in one day of a single bug class, an input that changes how a take SOUNDS without changing the identity of the take, and duplicating the key is what let it recur, so take_path() is now the only definition.

entries.upgrade: scripts/gen_captions_ts.py: the caption cue file is GENERATED from vo_lines.json rather than hand-typed, and --check fails a run whose committed cues are not what the current takes produce. Case0002's shot ladder became CUT_ON, a list of cue INDICES, and Root.tsx derives durationInFrames from the VO total.
entries.verified_by: python3 scripts/gen_captions_ts.py --self-test -> exit 0, seven cases including a RED one for a cue file that no longer matches the takes. One case initially passed for the WRONG reason (counting 'who: ' matched the Cue type declaration as well as the cues) and was tightened to 'who: ' with the quote, which is the kind of false green this gate exists to prevent. Generated for case 2, then --check confirmed current. npx tsc --noEmit -p video-engine -> exit 0 after both the composition and Root.tsx changes. Twenty-odd hand-entered numbers described one thing, re-synthesis moved all of them, and they were retyped twice in one day; a stale one cannot be seen in a render because the file stays internally consistent and the picture simply cuts on the wrong word.

entries.upgrade: scripts/vo_soundcheck.py: a listening gate, so voice quality stops depending on a human playing the file back. Measures duration, gross and articulation rate, F0 variance and range, dynamics, pauses, peak and slot overrun per line and for a whole episode.
entries.verified_by: python3 scripts/vo_soundcheck.py --self-test -> exit 0, six fixtures, five of them RED on purpose (sedated, gabbling, dead, clipping, and a take that read its direction as dialogue) and one clean case green. IMPORTANT, and the reason this gate is deliberately narrow: an earlier cut judged PROSODY, and measurement against the owner's own ranking FALSIFIED it. The take called horrid scored the HIGHEST pitch variance (3.79 semitones) and the widest dynamics (18.1 dB); the take the owner liked scored the LOWEST on both (1.42, 10.7). A slower take (1.92 w/s) was also preferred over a faster one (2.83). So the gate now hard-fails only measurable MALFUNCTION and prints prosody as information it refuses to grade. The falsification table is in the file header so the next engineer cannot re-derive the thresholds that were already disproven.

entries.upgrade: Editorial register: the show is written for adults. Three standing beats added (the-grift, the-vice, the-landlord), sources.yaml gained a WHAT A STORY HAS TO HAVE (TEETH) section, and the funny gate now asks whether an episode has teeth and CAPS AT 70 when it does not. The hard line is stated in the same breath as the licence, so pushing to it does not read as permission to cross it.
entries.verified_by: Both config files parse (python3 -c yaml.safe_load on sources.yaml and scoring_rubric.yaml). The ban list is restated verbatim and unchanged in all three knowledge files: no slurs, no hate, no sexual content, no harassment, institutions and public figures only, never private individuals or protected classes. UNPROVEN AS OF THIS COMMIT: the three new beats have never sourced a story. Case 0003 is their first test and the thing to watch is whether teeth arrives as a real sourced claim or as an adjective the writer reaches for.

entries.upgrade: Staging and speaker identification in video-engine/src/Case0002.tsx: a per-speaker caption tint plus a speaker label, binary talk poses driven by speakerAt(), a seven-beat shot ladder replacing the head-on two-shot the storyboard critic flagged eight times, and a parallax rate so the push reads as a camera move.
entries.verified_by: Rendered and inspected, not asserted. The rebuilt episode renders clean at 1080x1920, 48.87s, and the caption cue file now carries `who` per cue with speakerAt(t) exported from one place, so the tint, the label and the talk pose cannot disagree with each other. The storyboard critic's blocker from the shipped run (a dark-red arc across Ray's legs, root-caused to the flannel plaid's third stripe drawn outside the coat silhouette) was fixed in the RIG in lib/Character.tsx, so it is fixed for every flannel character in every future episode rather than for one shot.

entries.upgrade: THE FUNNY GATE WAS IN THE WRONG PHASE. scripts/retro.py gives the machine cross-run memory of every critic verdict and escalates any defect seen in 2+ runs from a script problem to a PROCESS problem, naming the phase that OWNS the decision. scripts/story_check.py is the upgrade that finding demanded: a PHASE 3 gate that refuses a story whose absurdity cannot be written down as a mechanism.
entries.verified_by: retro.py --self-test exit 0, six cases, including RED for an unaddressed repeat offender and GREEN only once a shipped upgrade claims it. story_check.py --self-test exit 0, six cases, five RED. Backfilled all nine real verdicts from cases 0002 and 0003, which is what turned 'the critic keeps complaining' into evidence: agreement_not_comedy, carried_by_fact and button_doesnt_land each appear in BOTH runs. Run against case 0003's story as it was actually conceived, story_check FAILS on 'the company' not being a person to act out and on 'it is unfair' not being a reason. The act-out requirement is not arbitrary: 'somebody hit paste twice' was the only line either critic called a real joke across six reads, and requiring a PERSON at Phase 3 forces that framing before a script exists.

entries.upgrade: THE BUTTON HAD NO OWNER. `button_doesnt_land` recurred across cases 0002 and 0003 and every response was to rewrite the last line, which is the artifact and not the decision. Nothing in the machine chose the button until the writer reached the end of a draft, so it was structurally an afterthought and the ending was always the one the viewer already had queued. PHASE 3.7, the producer room, now names the button BEFORE a line is written: its document, its image, and why Ray does not win. That plan binds every later phase, and the director at 4.4 can reject a script whose turn or button cannot be illustrated. The button is now a decision with a phase, an owner and a downstream veto.
entries.verified_by: retro.py --check exits 0 with every repeat offender claimed; retro.py --self-test exit 0 both directions; producer plan schema carries the_button {document, image, why_ray_does_not_win} as required fields; routine Phase 3.7 spawns producer before Phase 4.

entries.upgrade: THE FIRST END-TO-END DRY RUN OF THE NEW ROOMS, and it paid for itself in defects found. Ran Phase 3 -> 3.7 -> 4 -> 4.2 -> 4.4 -> 4.5 against a fixture, then re-ran 3.7 against the real cleared claims. Every phase fired, and every phase found something the phase before it got wrong. Shipped fixes: (1) scripts/coherence_check.py, a new gate catching the plan and the world describing different films, which two agents found independently and no human noticed; it shipped WITH the bug of passing on silence and was fixed the same run. (2) visual_check crashed on a world written as a string instead of an object, which is the shorthand a human writes; a gate that crashes is worse than one that misses because it prints a traceback instead of a report. (3) WORLD_KIT's warning that zero of thirteen primitives are built was one buried line and the producer walked straight into it, budgeting three props for 100 percent new construction; hoisted to the top of the file. (4) A KILL is now a WORK LIST that re-enters an editing loop, per the owner, matching the show's own law that a gate failure ends an attempt and never the run. (5) A reject now names where it goes; the director nearly sent thirteen serviceable lines back to the writers room for a producer's error. (6) Two new retro slugs, beautiful_and_unfunny and artifacts_fork, because the taxonomy could not name a set that is doing everything and still is not funny. (7) Schema fixes in producer, designer, writer and director specs, all found by the agents in their own specs, the most important being beats[].claims, since a beat with no claim binding is a beat nobody can check and that is the exact failure that already cost this show an episode.
entries.verified_by: Every gate self-tests both directions and every gate verified against an EMPTY document, which is how the coherence bug was caught: story_check, visual_check, coherence_check all exit 1 on empty and on blank-but-present. visual_check verified on real content in both directions: 11 red rows on a talking-heads board, 16 of 16 green on a good one, both kept in knowledge/examples/. retro --check exits 0. refs_check clean, 29 files.

entries.upgrade: script_check gains a RESTATEMENT guard, closing the standing repeat offender `explaining_lines`. The funny critic named it on case 0003 in two separate runs and CAST_BIBLE has banned it in prose since the start ("nothing explains a joke that already landed"), which is exactly the shape retro.py exists to escalate: a rule enforced only by a critic reading the draft afterwards is not enforced, because the critic is downstream of the decision. The guard fires when a line's content words are >=60% contained in the line immediately above it AND it cites no claim that line did not already carry. Deliberately narrow: INSTITUTION and verbatim lines are exempt (policy text repeating itself is the JOKE), and lines under two content words are exempt ("Okay." reacts, it does not restate). A guard that fires on taste gets switched off, so this one only fires on the restatement SHAPE.
entries.verified_by: Self-test case added that trips ONLY this guard (both lines are Ray's, at 30.0 and 34.0, inside the middle third and inside every Ray-gap bound, so no neighbouring guard can cover for it). MUTATION-TESTED per the repo's oldest law: neutering the threshold to 99.0 makes the self-test print 'did NOT fire: [restates]' and 'THE GATE IS WRONG', and restoring it goes green again. Also run against the real case 0003 script, where it is clean: it does NOT fire on "He got sued once.", the line the funny critic wanted cut and the simulated viewer LAUGHED at, which is the false positive this design was shaped to avoid.

entries.upgrade: contact_sheet: 12 cells -> 24, 4 cols -> 6, and the SAMPLING INTERVAL is now printed on the sheet itself. Twelve cells across 58s is one frame every 4.8s, and on case 0003 that interval produced two confidently WRONG critic findings in a single round: the flow critic reported the eight stacked head lines as 'not in the render' and the storyboard critic made `pile-never-rendered` its single systemic finding. Both beats render fine, at 22.2s, 31.0s and 48.5s, in windows the sheet never sampled. The critics were not careless; a grid does not LOOK sampled, it looks complete, so a gap reads as an absence. The caveat therefore ships ON the artifact the critic reads, not in a prompt they may not get.
entries.verified_by: Module parses and --help reports the new defaults. The defect itself was proven empirically first: nine extra frames pulled from the SHIPPED mp4 at 19.5/22.2/25.5/27.6/29.0/31.0/34.5/45.0/48.5s show the eight identical head lines, the VERIFIED emboss, both figures full-frame in a clean two-shot, and the RESOLVED-vs-INVALID payoff, refuting both findings.
